marcadores.explicacao_original: Mucus-secreting tubules can be distinguished by their pale staining, frothy appearance. The lumens of these tubules are larger than those of acini, allowing passage of the thicker secretory product the tubules produce.

marcadores.explicacao_original: Serous-secreting acini stain more intensely than do the tubules. Acini resemble grapefruits cut in cross section, with each grapefruit wedge representing an individual cell. Secretory granules fill the apex of each cell, lying adjacent to the acinar lumen into which they will be released. The lumen of each acinus is smaller than that of a tubule.
